facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 火_偏印 (Fire carrying The Alchemist). Persona The Alchemist (偏印). Definition line: "Unconventional nourishment, the insight that transmutes". Keyword Insight, charge fierce, poles catalyst Vision / friction Distance. Family function: Mind. Cost dimension: nourishment that transmutes; fed on strange food, recipe unshareable. Arena: crucible, moon-side, distillation, the changed substance. Classical portrait: unorthodox absorption; solitary mastery; intake that starves output (枭神夺食). Ruled domains: Learning, Intuition, Solitude. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 正印.
Element arena: Fire (flame, light, warmth, fuel, the hearth, the blaze). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Earth. structural_interaction seed: "Fire generating Earth same-polarity — warmth as activation source for stability".
- k2_overview: "Your Fire moves as the Alchemist: illumination in a closed vessel. Your insight comes in flashes, sudden clarity that lights a whole cavern, then dims while you sketch what you saw. You understand things sideways, by vision rather than proof. Keep notebooks. The flashes are real, and unrecorded lightning teaches no one."
- k2_functional: "You think in flashes: whole answers arriving lit, proofs assembled after."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Obsessive","Erratic","Distant"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Learning":"You learn by ignition: nothing for weeks, then a spark takes and you consume a field in days. Honor the cycle. Keep fuel stacked for when the flash comes.","Intuition":"Your intuition arrives as vision: sudden, whole, and correct more often than you can justify. Note it immediately. The flash fades faster than the truth it showed.","Solitude":"Your solitude is the dark that makes flashes visible: crowds wash out your signal. Reserve real darkness, evenings unplugged, questions held alone. Then carry the light out."}
- fn_reading.catalyst.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.catalyst; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 火_正印 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Warm-hearted","Encouraging","Healing"],"friction":["Babying","Dependent","Drowsy"]}
- Sibling cell 火_正印 catalyst row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Your presence is the warm center other lives arrange themselves around. People come in from their cold weeks and hold their hands out to you, mostly without noticing the gesture. The warmth is steady, unconditional, and quietly expensive to maintain. Nobody sees the fuel line. You are the fuel line."

Core element Earth, energy element Fire. Law: Fire feeds Earth (火生土: ash becomes soil). Relative to the core the energy is the feeder, so Fire is this core's Mind. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Earth core that shows Fire on the catalyst pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The catalyst pole of Fire as the Mind is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: compliment. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 土_火's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: You see the whole answer first and work out the steps after. You need the shape of a thing before its parts, so you trust what you saw rather than what you can prove. Take the whole picture seriously and let the proof catch up.

value_b.text: You get whole answers, with the reasons arriving later. Taking a thing in piece by piece leaves you lost, and you trust the complete view more than any single step. When you say it unproven, you have the picture tested while it is fresh.

value.text: Seeing it whole is how you know a thing is true. Because you want proof to show, you sit on the picture rather than use it. If you act on what you see early, you keep the head start that waiting throws away.

value.text: Most of what you know, you taught yourself. You own a thing only once you work it out alone, so you would rather find your own way than take a course. Teach yourself the dull basics too, to keep your knowledge free of holes.

value_b.text: You learn best as your own teacher. An answer you were taught never feels yours, and you teach it to yourself instead of taking the lesson. Put what you find on paper, where it counts outside your own head.

value.text: Self-taught is the only learning you trust. Because a thing has to be found before it feels true, you spend months finding it alone rather than an hour being told. Whenever a lesson would spare you the search, take it and keep those months.

value.text: Your best thinking happens with nobody else in it. You need quiet to hear your own thinking, so you take a question away to think it through rather than talk it out. Set that quiet aside before you have to think in a crowd.

value_b.text: You think most clearly alone. Since answering on the spot feels like guessing, you would rather think a thing over alone than give a quick reply. If a question matters, take a day to think and bring back an answer you trust.

value.text: When something weighs on you, you think it through alone first. Because talking before you have an answer feels unsafe, you carry the worry alone rather than share it. Let one person into your thinking to get the comfort you now go without.

value.text: Working something out, you go quiet on everyone around you. Because you think best alone rather than with others, you leave the people beside you on their own. When you need to think, say it first and stay close enough to be good company.
